definitions.gloss: to crouch down; to squat down; to huddle up
definitions.explanation: To bend the body low and curl up close to the ground. Often implies being in pain, feeling cold, or trying to hide. Can also be written as 蹲る in kanji.

examples.japanese: {道端|みちばた}でうずくまっている{人|ひと}がいた。
examples.english: There was a person crouching on the side of the road.

examples.japanese: おなかが{痛|いた}くてうずくまった。
examples.english: I crouched down because of a stomachache.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}さに{耐|た}えきれず、{壁際|かべぎわ}にうずくまって{体|からだ}を{丸|まる}めた。
examples.english: Unable to bear the cold, I huddled against the wall and curled up.

notes:
USAGE:
Usually written in hiragana. The kanji form {蹲|うずくま}る exists but is rarely used. Often describes someone who is in distress (pain, cold, exhaustion) and sinks to the ground, or an animal making itself small.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道端|みちばた}にうずくまる (to crouch on the roadside)
- うずくまって{泣|な}く (to cry while crouched down)
- {地面|じめん}にうずくまる (to crouch on the ground)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- しゃがむ: to squat — a more casual or purposeful squatting position
- かがむ: to bend down — bending forward, not necessarily curling up
